Hi there—thank you so much for coming in today. My name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I specialize in the emotional well-being of new mothers, and I’m really glad you’re here.

Over the next few minutes I’d like to complete the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—often called the EPDS—with you. It’s a short, 10-question screening that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally in the past seven days. It isn’t a test of your mothering; it’s simply a tool that lets us see if you might benefit from extra support right now.

Everything you share is confidential. My goal is to create a safe, non-judgmental space where you can be honest without worrying about anyone’s expectations. We’ll go through each question one at a time, and you can answer in your own words—no need to worry about choosing from a list.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first question:

Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I’ve noticed that laughing feels kind of distant lately. Like, if my husband shows me a funny video, I might smile for a second, but it fades quickly and I’m back to feeling heavy. I used to laugh easily—now it’s like the joy just doesn’t stick.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I can laugh a little, but most of the time it feels forced—like I’m just pretending because I know I should enjoy the moment. The humor doesn’t reach me the way it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I try to tell myself I should be excited about little outings—like when my mom offers to drive me and the baby to the park—but honestly, when the time comes, I just feel kind of flat. Even coffee with a friend feels like another chore I have to get through, not something I actually look forward to.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… if the baby spits up a lot or won’t settle, I keep thinking it must be something I’m doing wrong—like I’m not feeding him right or I’m missing some cue. I’ll replay every little thing in my head and tell myself a better mom would know how to fix it.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be sitting there, baby’s asleep and nothing’s actually wrong, but my chest feels tight and I’m scanning the room for dangers—what if the swaddle’s too loose, what if the monitor stops working, what if he suddenly stops breathing? I know it sounds dramatic, but I can’t shake the “what-ifs,” even when everything looks fine.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah, it’s happened a few times this week. I’ll be folding laundry or warming a bottle and suddenly my heart’s racing, I feel shaky, and I have to sit down because I’m sure something awful is about to happen—even though I can’t name what it is. It passes after a bit, but it leaves me exhausted.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It feels like as soon as I finish one feeding, the next is due, the diapers pile up, and I can’t even get a shower in. I keep thinking, “I’m barely holding this together,” and sometimes I have to put the baby in the crib for a minute and walk away so I can breathe.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I lie down exhausted, but my head won’t stop spinning—did I wash the bottles, is the baby breathing, am I already failing him? Some nights I’m still awake at two or three, and when I do drift off, every squeak from the bassinet jolts me awake again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling—like I’m already behind before I even open my eyes. I look at my baby and feel guilty because I want to be happy for him, but mostly I just feel empty and on the verge of tears.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened a few times this week. Sometimes it’s because I’m frustrated—he won’t latch or I spill pumped milk—but other times it’s for no clear reason at all. I’ll just be sitting on the couch and the tears start rolling, and I can’t seem to turn them off.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t thought about hurting myself. I do feel overwhelmed and pretty low, but I’ve never wanted to harm myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – 2 wks PP

<sym>Symptoms endorsed</sym>
- Persistent low mood, daily tearfulness, anhedonia
- Marked guilt/self-blame regarding infant care
- Heightened, ill-defined anxiety with panic spells (racing heart, shakiness)
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia linked to ruminative worry
- Sense of being overwhelmed, “barely holding it together”

<med>Pattern</med>: Symptoms present most days, interfere with functioning; no self-harm ideation reported.

<med>Screening significance</med>
- Meets threshold indicators for Major Depressive Episode (postpartum onset) and comorbid anxiety
- No current safety concerns (denies suicidal/homicidal thoughts, plan, or intent)

Plan: Recommend urgent follow-up with OB/midwife and formal mental health evaluation for diagnostic clarification and treatment discussion.
